question: Should OpenClaw implement immutable operator policy as a core runtime enforcement layer, or keep policy files as conformance/audit inputs with Nix-owned immutability for declarative installs?
rationale: The requested behavior changes config precedence, write authorization, diagnostics, and security ownership; current main has adjacent audit/conformance surfaces but no maintainer-approved runtime lock boundary.

options.title: Implement core immutable overlay
options.body: Define a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, config-write conflict rejection, status/doctor visibility, focused tests, docs, and upgrade guidance.

options.title: Keep policy conformance-only
options.body: Document that operators should use Policy checks, policy compare, attestations, and Nix-managed config for immutable baselines while runtime config remains mutable.

options.title: Defer for hook design
options.body: Wait for the related policy-hook proposals to settle whether enforcement should be owned by plugin hooks or core config/write paths.

recommendation.title: Implement core immutable overlay
recommendation.body: Define a startup-loaded operator policy source with locked precedence, config-write conflict rejection, status/doctor visibility, focused tests, docs, and upgrade guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the issue and authored the prior exact implementation candidate.
